facts.fact: Since 3 August 2026 Congolese taxpayers can pay taxes, levies and customs duties online through the Fouta national switch after filing on the E-Tax or Sydonia platforms, with an electronic Treasury receipt issued, according to L'Economie.
The Fouta pilot with firms already used to e-filing is complete and rollout is progressive, to large then medium companies and to all taxpayers by the end of 2026, according to L'Economie.

facts.fact: Minister Christian Yoka said the Fouta platform collected 107 billion FCFA from its launch on 1 June to 16 November 2026, through seven banks.
The ministry says 94 billion FCFA came from taxes through the e-Tax online filing and payment system and 13 billion from duties and taxes through Sydonia customs.
The ministry says revenue collected through Fouta equals 8.5% of 2026 tax revenue, 107 billion FCFA by 16 November.
Finance minister Christian Yoka told the National Assembly that the FOUTA platform, launched on 1 June 2026, collects public revenue through seven named banks, with MUCODEC and UBA to join.
Yoka said FOUTA is the single payment and collection channel for customs revenue through SYDONIA and tax revenue through e-Tax, as well as forestry, oil, administrative and domain revenue.
Yoka said FOUTA had collected nearly FCFA 107 billion by 16 November 2026, FCFA 94 billion through e-Tax and FCFA 13 billion through SYDONIA, against about FCFA 1 billion for its predecessor e-Pay.
